new_statements.rule_in_words: In the only record of the language (Bartlett's ca. 1862 vocabulary in Spanish orthography), word stress falls on the final syllable, marked there by an acute accent; Shaul tabulates Robinia stress as 'final', hedging that items written without an accent may have had penultimate stress and that apparent root-stress contrasts are artifacts of position. Gatschet 1877:388, who first published the manuscript, independently says the words 'have the word accent mostly on the final syllable' (den Wortton zumeist auf der Endsilbe).
new_statements.exceptions: Shaul: forms recorded without an accent mark are 'perhaps' penultimately stressed; putative minimal stress pairs (bu/bú, ka/ká, u-/ú) are dismissed as artifacts of final vs. non-final position. Gatschet: 'zumeist' (mostly) final, no exceptions itemised.
new_statements.domain_note: Citation forms in a ca. 150-item wordlist (single words and short compounds) written by a non-linguist in Spanish orthography ca. 1862 and published by Gatschet 1877; no phrase or sentence data exist, so the domain is the isolated word. The whole corpus is this one vocabulary; the statement rests on its accent marks.
new_statements.identity_note: The entire record of 'Robinia' is one vocabulary (ca. 150 items) in J. R. Bartlett's manuscript (NAA MS 1132, ca. 1862), published by Gatschet 1877:390-418 as a 'Cochimí' column and later called 'Cochimí II' (Troike 1976) / 'Bartlett's Cochimi from Mr. Robinia' (Glottolog). Provenance is described inconsistently: Gatschet 1877:388 says Bartlett obtained it 'durch Herrn Robinia aus Guaymas in Sonora' (an intermediary, how he got it 'wird nicht gesagt'); Glottolog says it was collected 'from a man called Robinia'; Shaul 2020 calls Robinia Bartlett's 'consultant' and says the language was 'recorded from a speaker in Hermosillo, Sonora'. All agree the language itself belonged to the northern third of the Baja California peninsula and is distinct from Cochimí proper (coch1272; 34% shared vocabulary). The stress statements quoted apply to this vocabulary only; Gatschet's separate remarks on p. 387-388 ('oxytonirt'; Wortton auf die letzte Silbe in Clavigero's prayers) concern Cochimí proper, not Robinia.
